primary_speaker: unnamed coach (Google Business Profile verification expert)

frameworks.name: Three-Factor Instant Verification Trust Model
frameworks.definition: Google trusts established Gmail accounts, devices, and previous activity; instant verification requires a combination of all three factors working in alignment.

claims.text: Aged Gmail accounts with 5+ years of activity (Google Maps use, YouTube searches, YouTube Premium purchases) receive instant Google Business Profile verification; new Gmail accounts created immediately before attempting verification have ~0% success rate.
claims.speaker: unnamed coach
conditions: Google Business Profile creation via Gmail
no prior verification attempts on account
claims.mechanism: Google recognizes long-term account activity as a trust signal of legitimacy rather than spam

numbers.axis: Gmail account age and verification success

anchors.region: aged account 5+ years with active use

bounded_by: Does not apply to recycled/purchased Gmail accounts (marked as fake by Google)
Easier for low-liability service categories (cleaning, detailing) than regulated ones (plumbing, licensed services)

claims.text: Using the same Gmail account to attempt verification on multiple devices in quick succession, all on the same Wi-Fi, triggers Google spam detection; different devices flag the attempt as artificial batch account creation.
claims.speaker: unnamed coach
conditions: multiple verification attempts on single Gmail account
claims.mechanism: Google pattern-matches rapid cross-device attempts from same IP and account to automated mass-verification botnets
bounded_by: Does not apply to legitimate sequential business profile creation over time

claims.text: A Gmail account that has already created one Google Business Profile will require explicit verification (code, video, email) for any subsequent profile creation on the same account.
claims.speaker: unnamed coach
conditions: second or subsequent profile creation attempt on same Gmail

claims.text: Creating multiple Google Business Profiles across different service areas and geographic regions, using a rotating pool of aged family and friend Gmail accounts plus different devices, enables reliable instant verification at scale without submitting video or phone-code identity verification.
claims.speaker: unnamed coach
conditions: access to 3+ trusted aged Gmail accounts
claims.mechanism: Distributing verification attempts across distinct account-device pairs breaks the pattern that triggers Google's spam detection
bounded_by: Becomes harder to scale with regulated service categories requiring licensing or bonding

claims.text: The ease of instant Google Business Profile verification correlates inversely with regulatory liability: cleaning and landscaping verify near-instantly with aged Gmail accounts, while plumbing (licensed, bonded) requires additional verification friction.
claims.speaker: unnamed coach
claims.mechanism: Low-liability service categories face lower fraud risk in Google's categorization model; licensed categories require proof of legitimacy

claims.text: The speaker generates $20-30k monthly by listing verified Google Business Profiles across multiple service areas, qualifying leads from those profiles, and either selling leads directly or contracting the service work internally.
claims.speaker: unnamed coach
claims.mechanism: Instant verification at scale reduces lead-acquisition friction; high-volume lead aggregation from multiple profiles multiplies monthly revenue

numbers.axis: monthly revenue from Google Business Profile lead arbitrage

examples.text: The speaker demonstrates instant verification on video by filling in business details (address, hours, services), submitting the form, and receiving immediate 'you are now verified' confirmation on a plumbing business profile, all without video or code submission. The verified status appears as a checkmark next to the business name in the profile picture area.

The speaker uses a stranger's phone at a shopping mall, offering $10 cash incentive to demonstrate the instant-verification tactic in real-time. The stranger's aged Gmail account (with Google storage purchase history visible as a ring around profile picture) verifies a plumbing business profile instantly upon submission, with no additional friction.

The speaker owns multiple Google Business Profiles across different cities and service categories (clearly stating 'you manage this business profile' on several profiles visible in management console), demonstrating the portfolio approach to lead generation and fulfillment.

practices.text: Ask family members, friends, or acquaintances if you can use their aged Gmail account to create a Google Business Profile; prioritize accounts with 5+ years of activity.
Use different devices for each verification attempt (e.g., phone for one attempt, computer for another); avoid using the same device on the same Wi-Fi network for multiple rapid attempts.

Do not purchase aged Gmail accounts from third-party sellers; use trusted personal accounts only because purchased accounts are often recycled or created in bulk outside the US (increasing spam-filter risk).
Target service categories with low regulatory liability (cleaning, landscaping, detailing) before attempting categories requiring licensing or bonding (plumbing, electrical).

To scale lead generation, pay young people ($10 per attempt is mentioned as viable) to use their phones for verification attempts; college campuses and social networks are cited as recruiting sources.
